Duniya mein log dhoop aur baarish se bachne ke liye 50 rupaye ki chhatri khareed lete hain, lekin in bhai sahab ka alag hi level ka junoon chal raha hai! 

In this video, we explore the incredible 7,400-year-old ancient art of crafting the traditional Douli (斗笠) — an ancient Chinese waterproof conical bamboo hat recognized as National Intangible Cultural Heritage. But watch what happens when extreme craftsmanship meets pure cinematic drama! 

From tracking down a specific 3-year-old bamboo stalk in the deep wilderness to slicing bamboo fibers thinner than noodles and literally climbing a 5,000-foot mountain peak just to weave the geometric lattice in the clouds, this artisan takes dedication to a whole new level. And just when you think you've seen it all, watch his unbelievable waterproof test under a freezing waterfall wearing a full straw rain cloak and playing a bamboo flute!

⚽ FIFA World Cup Messi-Ronaldo 😍 Women’s T20 World Cup Bhi  
FIFA World Cup ka excitement poori duniya mein chhaya hua hai aur football fans ke liye yeh kisi festival se kam nahi hai. ⚽🔥 Is khaas mauke par Lionel Messi aur Cristiano Ronaldo ek saath baithe nazar aaye, jise dekhkar football lovers ka excitement aur bhi badh gaya.

India mein bhi football ki popularity lagatar badh rahi hai. Kai Indian sports fans FIFA World Cup, Messi aur Ronaldo ko follow karte hain. Indian cricket superstar Virat Kohli bhi football ke bade fan maane jaate hain aur kai baar football ke prati apna pyaar zahir kar chuke hain.

Football ke saath-saath cricket fans ke liye bhi badi khushkhabri hai, kyunki Women’s T20 World Cup bhi jald shuru hone wala hai. Sabki nazrein star players Smriti Mandhana, Harmanpreet Kaur aur Ellyse Perry par hongi, jo apni teams ke liye shandaar pradarshan karne ke liye taiyar hain. 🏏✨

Ek taraf FIFA World Cup ka junoon, doosri taraf Women’s T20 World Cup ka romanch — sports fans ke liye yeh samay sach mein bahut khaas hai.

snippet.title: Ice Destroyed the First Kerch Bridge. Russia Built the Next One Further South
snippet.description:
The Crimean Bridge crosses the Kerch Strait from Russia's Taman peninsula to Crimea, the peninsula Russia seized from Ukraine in 2014. At its narrowest the strait is less than three miles wide, but a Soviet railway bridge built there in 1944 lasted only months before ice from the Sea of Azov tore it down. Today's bridge runs further south over Tuzla island and a long dam, and every other road onto Crimea comes from mainland Ukraine.
Where would you have built it?
